title: yadgar/project
$comment: Closure is per chart (ADR-0850): this schema closes only the keys this chart owns; it does not close any chart's keys but its own. Every value stays untyped (no `type`, `enum`, `default` or `required`) — a toggle's type, a boolean, and every cross-key rule are `templates/render-checks.yaml`'s job (ADR-0797, ADR-0847), not the schema's — WITH TWO NAMED EXCEPTIONS: `tls.enabled` and `projectDb.tls.enabled` carry `type: boolean` and `required` (ADR-0845), and `tls.clientAuth` carries `required` ALONE, untyped (B-U5, ADR-0845 as extended to the client-auth knob). ADR-0845 states that these two knobs have no default anywhere, including a chart default, so the schema itself refuses an absent, null or non-boolean value rather than leaving that to the render check (measured: this chart ships no default for either key to begin with, so a null and a never-declared key both collapse to the same `required` refusal). `templates/render-checks.yaml`'s own `hasKey`/`kindIs "bool"` arms for these same two leaves stay in the template for `--disable-openapi-validation` but are unreachable on the normal `helm template`/`helm install` path, where the schema answers first; what that template guard actually owns is `tls`/`projectDb.tls` ITSELF being null or not a map, which this schema's nested `properties`/`required` never inspects at all. `tls.clientAuth` has no default anywhere: the binary reads LISTEN_TLS_CLIENT_AUTH whether or not TLS is on and refuses the boot without it, so the schema refuses an absent value. Its SHAPE is deliberately NOT typed here (no `enum`, no `type`; ADR-0847): a bare YAML `off` is the boolean false, and the render check's named sentence — `write clientAuth: "off", quoted` — is what an operator must read, which a schema type would pre-empt. `templates/render-checks.yaml` refuses a non-string or a value outside off/optional/required. `tls.clientCaSecret` and `tls.clientCaSecretKey` stay untyped and optional: the render check requires `clientCaSecret` only for a verifying mode. Open maps, declared `{}` on purpose: `global` is the block the parent forwards to every module and the parent (not this chart) closes it; `resources` and `rollingUpdate` are bare Kubernetes maps whose optional sub-keys (e.g. `resources.requests.ephemeral-storage`) this chart never names, so an adopter is free to set any of them. Extras — keys a template reads that `values.yaml` does not declare, so declaring them here closes their parent block rather than leaving it open: `image.digest` is written by ci-release at package time (D65) and is absent from the committed `values.yaml`, which ships only `repository` and `tag`; `networkPolicy.scrapeFrom.namespace` is the one key an adopter sets under the `scrapeFrom: {}` this chart ships empty, to admit the metrics scrape (D54).
